title: Transmission / CVT Common Issues
subtitle: Shudder, slip, delayed engagement — we'll triage safely and know when fluid DIY stops and a specialist starts.
tone: Production EN coach (US/EU): warm mentor, visual-first, max 2 CTAs, progress %, mileage personalization, legal disclaimer every step, high-risk modal with Find a nearby shop cancel. Phase 2 transmission: CVT-specific fluid rules; no 'miracle additives' as primary fix.

prerequisites: Know automatic vs CVT vs dual-clutch vs manual from the garage profile / manual
OBD reader helpful for transmission codes
Never ignore a vehicle that won't stay in gear on the road
tools_checklist: Optional: transmission fluid (OEM-only if DIY is approved)
parts_checklist: OEM-specified ATF / CVT fluid only (never 'universal' guesses)
Filter/pan gasket only if manual allows DIY service
No friction-modifier miracle bottles as a first fix

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Many models use belt/chain CVTs that need exact OEM fluid. Wrong fluid can destroy a CVT quickly.
CVT shudder on light acceleration is common in some models — diagnose with fluid history and codes before replacing the unit.
Dual-clutch (DCT) behavior differs from torque-converter automatics — 'slipping' at low speed can be normal clutch management. Still verify codes.
Past 100k, delayed engagement and burnt fluid smell deserve a specialist inspection before a long trip.
Most BEVs use a single-speed reduction gear — this playbook's AT/CVT fluid steps may not apply. Tell chat if you hear gear whine.
